From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: šuora

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *coora.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsuo̯rɑ/, [ˈs̠uo̞̯rɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -uorɑ
  • Syllabification(key): suo‧ra
  • Hyphenation(key): suo‧ra

Adjective

[edit]

suora (comparative suorempi, superlative suorin)

  1. straight, direct (not crooked, oblique or bent)
  2. straight, direct, truthful, frank, straightforward
  3. direct (immediate; express; plain; unambiguous)
  4. straight (having all cylinders in a single row)
  5. live (broadcast)
  6. right (of angle, 90°)

Usage notes

[edit]

A straight angle (180°) is oikokulma in Finnish.

Noun

[edit]

suora

  1. straight (something that is not crooked or bent, such as a part of a road or track that goes on straight)
  2. (geometry) line, straight line (infinitely extending one-dimensional figure that has no curvature)
  3. (poker) straight (five consecutive cards)
  4. (boxing) cross, straight

Italian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • suor (apocopic)
  • sora (Tuscan)[1]
  • suoro (archaic)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin soror (nominative) via loss of /-r/ and then adjustment of /-o/ to the more typical (for feminine nouns) /-a/.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈswɔ.ra/
  • Rhymes: -ɔra
  • Hyphenation: suò‧ra

Noun

[edit]

suora f (plural suore)

  1. nun
    Synonym: monaca
  2. (archaic) sister
    Synonym: sorella

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Ma'di: sụ́ẹrẹ̃
